title: Kicking off Cybersecurity Career Week with NIST!
text:
Official websites use .gov

Secure .gov websites use HTTPS

A lock (

Lock
A locked padlock

) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites.

Kicking off Cybersecurity Career Week with NIST!

October 14, 2026

By:
Susana Barraza

Credit:

NIST

Image info
Considering a career in cybersecurity? Cybersecurity Career Week (CCW), a campaign led by the NICE Program at NIST from October 19-24, 2026, aims to raise public awareness and help people find their path to #ChooseCyber. During this week, academia, industry, non-profit organizations, and government agencies host events, share resources, provide trainings, and engage community to build awareness about the cybersecurity job opportunities, educate people on how to develop capabilities to qualify for cybersecurity roles, and showcase how building a cybersecurity workforce enhances the Nation’s security and promotes economic prosperity.How to get startedBe ready to engage, explore, and try something new. Use CCW to ask questions, attend an event, connect with people already working in the field, or participate in challenges. You never know which conversation, activity, class, or resource might introduce you to your future cybersecurity career.To get started, visit the official CCW website to access global and local event listings, interactive toolkits, and free career planning resources. If you are an educator, mentor, or professional guiding others, the site also offers dedicated tools, and turnkey event guides to help you host activities and inspire the next generation of cybersecurity talent.Your cybersecurity career journey can start anywhere and at any time. The cybersecurity workforce needs people with a range of interests, experiences, strengths, and skills. Maybe you love solving problems, helping people, investigating how things work, communicating ideas, analyzing information, or building technology. During CCW you can find out about the variety of cybersecurity career options available and discover one that connects with your interests.Explore moreCybersecurity is much bigger than one job title. Discover resources like the NICE Framework to learn about different types of cybersecurity roles and what skills are needed. Check out CyberSeek(link is external) to learn more about what jobs are in demand, use the Cyber Career Pathways Tool from the National Initiative for Cybersecurity Careers and Studies to discover pathways, check out videos from practitioners, and see how different cybersecurity roles interconnect. Just click around and explore — you might be surprised by what you find!Remember, every career starts with a first step. Start small. Explore one career path. Ask one question. Learn one new skill. Make one connection. Share something you learned with someone else. CCW is about allowing yourself to be curious and discover where that curiosity might take you. Your path does not have to look like anyone else's — just keep exploring, learning, and moving forward. Happy CCW!Explore NIST’s CCW Events and Activities!Networking Like a Leader: Building Authentic Connections That Create Opportunities(Webinar)Wednesday, October 14, 2026 | 1:00 - 2:00 PM ETRegister HereNCCoE Cybersecurity Connections Event: National Cybersecurity Awareness Month (In-person event)Thursday, October 15, 2026 | 11:00 AM - 1:30 PM ETRegister HereChallenge: Six Day #mycyberjob Media Challenge October 19-24, 2026 X, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn and otherTag: @NISTCyberX Chat: NIST Chat #CyberCareerChat #CyberCareerWeek #MyCyberJobOct. 19, 2026 | 12:00-12:30 PM ET @NISTCyber and NICE partners will answer career questions and share resources. When the default self-signed certificate is used, an attacker could gain administrative access to the application.

title: CVE-2026-71854 - OpenAEV has unauthenticated access and missing object-level authorization on player lessons API
text:
8.2

HIGH
CVSS 3.1

CVE-2026-71854
OpenAEV has unauthenticated access and missing object-level authorization on player lessons API

OpenAEV is an open source platform allowing organizations to plan, schedule and conduct cyber adversary simulation campaign and tests. Prior to version 2.260622.0, on a default installation, the `/api/player/**` lessons endpoints can be called without authentication, and they trust a client-supplied `userId` query parameter without verifying that the caller is that user or a member of the exercise. An unauthenticated client that knows an exercise UUID can read lessons-learned questions and answers (including each answer's author identity) and create or overwrite answers attributed to an arbitrary user. Version 2.260622.0 contains a patch.

FileRise: WebDAV authentication bypasses TOTP/MFA entirely

FileRise is a self-hosted web-based file manager with multi-file upload, editing, and batch operations. text:
9.1

CRITICAL
CVSS 3.1

CVE-2026-85714
Stirling-PDF: Remote Code Execution via H2

Stirling-PDF is a locally hosted web application that facilitates various operations on PDF files. Prior to 2.13.2, an authenticated administrator using the default H2 database and security mode can upload a crafted SQL file to POST /api/v1/database/import-database. DatabaseService.validateSqlContent() splits normalized input on semicolons and accepts a statement when it contains any allowed keyword, allowing dangerous H2 functions such as FILE_READ and CSVWRITE, plus CREATE ALIAS, to bypass the insufficient whitelist and execute side effects when RUNSCRIPT processes the file. This permits arbitrary file access. The demonstrated operating-system command execution chain writes attacker-controlled startup files to a user-site location and then triggers an application Python interpreter configured to load those startup files, resulting in command execution as the JVM service account. This issue is fixed in version 2.13.2.

title: CVE-2026-63626 - Mongoose: ppp_handle_ipv6cp() uses attacker-controlled length without bounds check — OOB read and heap overflow (PPP/PPPoE, MG_ENABLE_IPV6)
text:
8.8

HIGH
CVSS 3.1

CVE-2026-63626
Mongoose: ppp_handle_ipv6cp() uses attacker-controlled length without bounds check — OOB read and heap overflow (PPP/PPPoE, MG_ENABLE_IPV6)

Mongoose is an embedded web server and network library. Prior to 7.23, ppp_handle_ipv6cp() in src/l2_ppp.c trusts the 16-bit IPv6CP len field without checking it against the received payload size. On a PPP or PPPoE link using MG_ENABLE_TCPIP and MG_ENABLE_IPV6, an unauthenticated adjacent peer can complete the required LCP exchange and send a short Configure-Request with an oversized length, causing ppp_tx_frame() to read beyond recv_queue.buf and write beyond tx.buf. The same length misuse can also expose adjacent heap bytes in a reply or hang the event loop through find_opt(). This issue is fixed in version 7.23.

CVE-2026-54525
Markdown Preview Enhanced: One Click RCE via Markdown Link Command Injection on Windows

Markdown Preview Enhanced is a Markdown preview extension for Visual Studio Code. Prior to 0.8.28, Markdown Preview Enhanced preview-link handling passes a decoded, Markdown-controlled link target to a Windows file-opening helper that invokes child_process.exec with the start command. When a Windows user opens an untrusted Markdown file and clicks a crafted external or unsupported-scheme link, shell metacharacters in the decoded target are interpreted by cmd.exe as command separators, allowing an attacker-selected command to run with the privileges of the current VS Code user. The attack requires one normal preview-link click but does not require malicious workspace configuration, script execution to be enabled, or additional files. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.28.

title: Ivanti ICS Zero-Day Attacks Highlight Vendor Patching Hurdles
text: Rob Wright,Senior News Director,Dark ReadingOctober 14, 20265 Min ReadSource: Florencio Horcajo Alvarez via Getty Images Even when technology vendors discover vulnerabilities before threat actors do, they can still fall victim to zero-day attacks.That's the unfortunate situation Ivanti found itself in this week, as attackers exploited two zero-day vulnerabilities in Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) products: a high-severity authentication bypass vulnerability and the follow-on ability for unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) in the SSL-VPN and remote-access gateway. The cybersecurity vendor yesterday disclosed both flaws collectively as CVE-2026-104935."We are aware of exploitation in the wild affecting a limited number of customers at the time of disclosure," Ivanti said in its advisory.But the situation is more complicated than your typical zero-day scenario. According to the advisory, Ivanti actually "discovered a portion of this vulnerability" in July through the vendor's product security program, and patched it with the ICS version 25.1.3.0 release. "We had been working to backport the fix to the remaining supported versions when exploitation occurred," Ivanti said. Volexity researchers discovered that a threat actor, tracked as UTA0576, was using a zero-day exploit chain earlier this month that included CVE-2026-104935. The chain compromised ICS appliances that were fully patched at the time.It's unclear what portion of CVE-2026-104935 Ivanti discovered over the summer, but an Ivanti spokesperson confirmed the discovery was made via Ivanti's LLM project, which uses several frontier and open source AI models to find and automatically remediate vulnerabilities in the company's products. But while AI models helped Ivanti get a head start on CVE-2026-104935, it appears threat actors were able to act even quicker.Loading... Multiple Zero-Days Exploited Against Ivanti ICS InstancesVolexity researchers first detected the malicious activity on Oct. 5 while investigating an incident at "a network security monitoring customer," according to a blog post published Tuesday. A forensic investigation revealed that an ICS appliance was the root cause of the attack that began on Oct. 3, and that UTA0576 used a zero-day exploit chain to compromise the device."This exploit chain combined an authentication bypass, a remote code execution (RCE), and a privilege escalation vulnerability to achieve unauthenticated root-level code execution" Volexity researchers wrote. "The RCE and authentication bypass vulnerabilities are tracked under CVE-2026-104935."The privilege escalation flaw has not been disclosed. Volexity said Ivanti is currently working on a fix for the vulnerability and it will be patched in a future update. UTA0576 actors extracted credentials from the ICS appliance and then engaged in a variety of post-compromise activities, from accessing the organization's Active Directory to deleting exploitation evidence from Ivanti debug logs. Volexity researchers said because the attack was detected and disrupted, it's unclear what UTA0576's ultimate objective was.What is clear, according to Douglas McKee, director of vulnerability intelligence at Rapid7, are the challenges facing vendors today for not just finding vulnerabilities before attackers do, but also fully addressing them before they can be exploited."Finding the bug is only part of the job," he tells Dark Reading. "Ivanti found a portion of this, fixed it in the newest release back in July, and then had to carry that same fix back across every older supported version still running in the field. That backport window is exactly where this went sideways, because the fix existed but hadn't reached everywhere it needed to be by the time attackers showed up."McKee emphasized that a quiet fix to one version could be a loud signal to attackers. "Attackers pay close attention to what a vendor changes, and an unpatched gap across supported versions is an open invitation to find the same […]

title: Cisco Warns of Active Attacks Exploiting New Critical Secure Email Gateway Vulnerability
text:
Cisco Warns of Active Attacks Exploiting New Critical Secure Email Gateway VulnerabilitySwati KhandelwalOct 14, 2026Email Security / Vulnerability

//<![CDATA[
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded",()=>{let t=document.querySelector("h1.story-title"),m=document.querySelector(".postmeta");t&&m&&t.insertAdjacentElement("afterend",m)})
//]]>

Attackers are exploiting a critical flaw in Cisco Secure Email Gateway that lets a sender with no login write files to the appliance's operating system, Cisco said in an advisory on Wednesday.

The attacker sends an email with a crafted attachment through the gateway and, if it succeeds, could then run commands as root. The appliance filters an organization's email for spam, malware, and other threats, and only a gateway with the File Reputation service enabled and a Content Scanner Tools package older than version 25.3.0.5525 is vulnerable.

The fix has been shipping since September 14 in AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 and 16.5.0-780, the builds Cisco listed as fixed in a hardening release that day, which the company now says covered this flaw. It also arrives as a Content Scanner Tools update, version 25.3.0.5525 or later, which installs without a software upgrade or a restart.

Cisco found the flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-76519 (CVSS score: 9.8), in its own internal security scanning and became aware of the attacks in October. The advisory does not say how many devices were attacked, who is behind the attacks, or whether the attackers obtained root on any of them.

Cisco has contacted customers of its managed Secure Email Cloud service whose devices showed "indicators of possible compromise" and says it is engaged in remediation and recovery. Administrators of those managed gateways may not have the command-line access needed to run the compromise check below, and Cisco has already deployed the fixed scanner there, so they need no action to get the fix.

Who Is Exposed

Both conditions must hold. The File Reputation service, part of the Advanced Malware Protection (AMP) feature that handles attachments, must be enabled and assigned to a mail policy, and the Content Scanner Tools version must be earlier than 25.3.0.5525.

Physical and virtual gateways on vulnerable AsyncOS releases are affected. Secure Email and Web Manager and Secure Web Appliance are not.

To check the first condition, open Mail Policies > Incoming Mail Policies > Advanced Malware Protection, or the same path under Outgoing Mail Policies, choose a mail policy, and look at the Enable File Reputation box. To check the second, run contentscannerstatus at the CLI, which shows the version and when it was last updated.

How to Fix It

The quickest route is the scanner update. Gateways with automatic Content Scanner Tools updates turned on need no action once the update has applied, so confirm with contentscannerstatus that the version is 25.3.0.5525 or later rather than assuming it arrived.

Where automatic updates are off, run contentscannerupdate at the CLI, or turn them on under Security Services > Service Updates.

The full AsyncOS fix is in these first fixed releases:

15.5: 15.5.5-014
16.0: no fixed build. Migrate to a fixed release.
16.5: 16.5.0-780
Content Scanner Tools (all licensed and supported AsyncOS releases): 25.3.0.5525 or later

Cisco recommends that any gateway earlier than 16.5 move to 16.5.0-780. A 16.0 gateway on 16.0.4-302, the build that fixed September's SQL injection flaw, is not fixed for this one, and the advisory does not list which releases count as licensed and supported for the scanner update. For a 16.0 gateway that stays on 16.0, the scanner version shown by contentscannerstatus is the only confirmation the advisory offers.

There is no workaround. For a virtual appliance that shows signs of compromise, Cisco's guidance is a rebuild with new credentials, and it warns that upgrading a compromised instance destroys the forensic data and logs.

How to Check for Compromise

title: Hackers Backdoor Nextcloud Servers Through Critical Flaw in Collabora’s Built-in CODE App
text:
Hackers Backdoor Nextcloud Servers Through Critical Flaw in Collabora’s Built-in CODE AppSwati KhandelwalOct 14, 2026Vulnerability / Malware

//<![CDATA[
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded",()=>{let t=document.querySelector("h1.story-title"),m=document.querySelector(".postmeta");t&&m&&t.insertAdjacentElement("afterend",m)})
//]]>

Attackers exploited a flaw in an optional Nextcloud app, Collabora Online - Built-in CODE Server, to plant web shells on Nextcloud servers. Three administrators reported the issue on GitHub, with the first logged attack on September 10.

A web shell is a small file that executes any command an attacker sends via a web request, with the rights of the web server account. The flaw allows an unauthenticated request to run a command on the server, but only when the app's local document server is not running, such as during a restart or upgrade, or after a crash.

Collabora fixed it in version 26.4.303 on September 11 and on October 14 published an advisory with the identifier CVE-2026-110447, warning that turning off the app does not help: it must be updated or removed.

Who Is Affected

The app, published by Collabora under the package name richdocumentscode, downloads a copy of Collabora Online Development Edition (CODE) and runs it on the Nextcloud server itself.

That lets Nextcloud Office edit documents without a separate Collabora server. Its store listing says it is "for local testing and non-production use" and "for personal use or for small teams."

Collabora's advisory covers every version before 26.4.303 and says standalone Collabora Online servers are not affected. A warning posted on the Nextcloud community forum on October 3 stated that an installation is not affected if it uses only the Nextcloud Office app ( richdocuments) without the built-in app, whether its Collabora server runs in Docker, from a Linux package, or at a hosting provider.

The app's proxy.php script starts the local CODE server whenever a request arrives, and nothing is listening. In versions up to 26.4.302, the script placed text from the request, including its path, inside a double-quoted bash command, where the shell still runs anything written as $(...).

A request with a command hidden in its path ran that command as the web server user. Because the script only builds that command when it needs to start the server, the attack works only while the server is down, such as during a container restart, an upgrade, or a crash.

The script is a plain PHP file that the web server runs directly from the app's folder and loads none of Nextcloud's code.

"It is not sufficient to disable the app to avoid the problem; it must be upgraded to >= 26.4.303 or removed," Collabora said in the advisory.

The fixed versions require Nextcloud 30 or later.

Nextcloud 29 and older are end of life, and the app store still serves them an affected version, so their users should upgrade Nextcloud or remove the app. Collabora's fix for a separate command-injection flaw in the same script, CVE-2025-66208, disclosed last December, does not prevent this one.

What the Attackers Did

The first report came from an administrator who hosts several Nextcloud servers and wrote on GitHub that the servers had been hacked since the day before. Access logs from two of them show requests at 19:51 on September 10 and 09:56 on September 11 (UTC+2), both from one IP address and both aimed at proxy.php?status with a shell command hidden in the request path. All of the administrator's servers ran version 26.4.302.

The command decoded a one-line PHP web shell into the app's folder and tried to send the server's uname -a output to a webhook.site address. On one server, the attacker then used the shell to search for credential stores and cryptocurrency wallets, including *.kdbx, wallet.dat and keystore.json files and names such as bitwarden, 1password, .bitcoin, .electrum, .monero and .ethereum.

The reviewed requests showed no commands that archived, […]

title: Highlights of Microsoft’s October Patch Release | Kaspersky official blog
text:
Microsoft’s October Patch Tuesday update stands out for two reasons. First, the total number of patches has reached four digits for the first time. Second, to help companies better understand the details of the vulnerabilities, Microsoft has decided to group them into risk cohorts. A cohort brings together vulnerabilities that are exploited under the same conditions and affect the same systems. They replace neither the severity rating, nor the individual bulletins for each CVE. While they’re unlikely to be suitable for comprehensive patch prioritization, they will help quickly assess which part of an infrastructure is currently most at risk.
Statistics corner
Of the 1,414 vulnerabilities addressed in the October Patch Tuesday release, 1,102 directly affect the Windows operating system, 134 — Microsoft Office, 36 — SharePoint Server, 22 — SQL Server, and seven — Exchange Server. The vast majority — 677 — lead to privilege escalation, 317 to remote code execution, 40 to security bypass, and 73 to denial of service (DoS).
There are 86 critical vulnerabilities on the list, of which 68 lead to RCE, 14 to privilege escalation, three to spoofing, and one to data leakage. In addition, two vulnerabilities were disclosed before being patched, and one is being exploited in real-world attacks.
CVE-2026-96951 — vulnerability in Windows Shell
The only zero-day vulnerability patched in the October update that attackers are already exploiting in real-world attacks is CVE-2026-96951 in Windows Shell (CVSS severity score: 8.8). Details on how it’s being exploited aren’t yet known; however, according to Microsoft’s description, it involves command injection that allows bypassing a security feature when accessing the system over a network. Microsoft credits experts at both Fujitsu and Anthropic for discovering the vulnerability, so it was likely found using neural networks.
CVE-2026-108398 and CVE-2026-92707: vulnerabilities disclosed before patches were released
Information about these two vulnerabilities was made public before the October update was released. In theory, this could mean that attackers attempted to exploit them ahead of time. These are:

CVE-2026-108398 — a vulnerability in the .NET Framework that allows bypassing WDAC protection;
CVE-2026-92707 — a vulnerability in the third-party MessagePack-CSharp serialization component, leading to a denial of service (DoS).

However, according to the security bulletins, neither has been observed in actual attacks yet.
What else to pay attention to
Several vulnerabilities patched by the latest update combine potentially serious consequences with relatively simple exploitation. Particular attention should be paid to three flaws that could potentially lead to arbitrary code execution:

CVE-2026-65674 (in SQL Server);
CVE-2026-70571 (in Exchange Server);
CVE-2026-70229 (in AD Domain Services).

What else should be patched?
Microsoft isn’t the only company that releases regular update packages for newly discovered vulnerabilities.
In its October update, Adobe fixed 174 defects in its products, including critical vulnerabilities (CVSS 10) in ColdFusion and Commerce/Magento. These systems are typically accessible from an external network, making them particularly attractive to attackers.
SAP’s October security bulletin lists 20 vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-89111 — an SSRF vulnerability in the Cloud SDK for Python. This vulnerability, rated CVSS 10, allows attackers to steal OAuth tokens.
How to keep your company safe?
Recently, thanks to neural networks, the number of vulnerabilities detected and patched has been regularly breaking records. To avoid getting overwhelmed by the flood of patches, we recommend using an automated platform for tracking and assessing vulnerabilities . It helps not only identify and fix vulnerabilities, it also prioritizes them based on actual risks and automates the remediation process.

title: Ahsay komt met update voor actief misbruikt lek in Cloud Backup Server
text:
Ahsay komt met update voor actief misbruikt lek in Cloud Backup Server

woensdag 14 oktober 2026, 15:36 door Redactie, 0 reacties

Softwareontwikkelaar Ashay heeft een hotfix uitgebracht voor een kwetsbaarheid waar aanvallers al zeker sinds 4 oktober misbruik van maken. Bij de aanvallen zijn meerdere organisaties gehackt. Ahsay Cloud Backup Server (CBS) is de management console voor de back-upsoftware van Ahsay. Het wordt voornamelijk gebruikt door managed serviceproviders (MSP's) en system integrators, om zo back-ups voor hun klanten te regelen. Zo is het mogelijk om back-upbeleid in te stellen, back-ups te maken en back-ups terug te zetten.

De oplossing bevat twee kwetsbaarheden (CVE-2026-105133 en CVE-2026-105134) die bij aanvallen zijn ingezet. CVE-2026-105133 is een 'authentication bypass' waardoor aanvallers de authenticatie kunnen omzeilen en toegang tot het AhsayCBS-systeem krijgen. CVE-2026-105134 maakt remote code execution met SYSTEM-rechten mogelijk. Bij de waargenomen aanvallen worden de twee kwetsbaarheden gecombineerd. Zodra aanvallers toegang tot een gecompromitteerde server hebben installeren ze webshells om toegang te behouden en verdere aanvallen uit te voeren.

Bij de aanvallen installeren de aanvallers ook cryptominers, die de rekenkracht van het systeem gebruiken voor het minen van cryptovaluta. De twee kwetsbaarheden werden gevonden door cybersecuritybedrijf Huntress, dat Ashay op 4 oktober inlichtte. Op 12 oktober maakte het softwarebedrijf melding dat er een hotfix is ontwikkeld. Deze hotfix verhelpt CVE-2026-105133, aldus Huntress. Daardoor kunnen aanvallers ook geen misbruik van CVE-2026-105134 maken, tenzij ze op het systeem weten in te loggen.

Het Nationaal Cyber Security Centrum (NCSC) adviseert om de beveiligingsupdates met spoed toe te passen en te onderzoeken of het systeem niet is gehackt. Na de installatie van de patch moet de server worden herstart. In het geval van een gehackt systeem raadt Ahsay aan om de server opnieuw op te bouwen en een schone configuratie terug te zetten.

The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Tuesday urged organizations to take steps to immediately update their Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) appliances and deployments to the latest version following the disclosure of an actively exploited vulnerability.

The security flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-104935 (CVSS score: 8.6), is a case of authentication bypass impacting ICS versions 25.1.1.1 and prior, 25.1.2.2 and prior, and 22.8R2.4 and prior that could allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary commands.

"CISA is aware of cyber threat actors exploiting this zero-day authentication bypass vulnerability, which allows remote, unauthenticated execution of arbitrary commands, to conduct credential theft and data exfiltration," the agency said.

The agency has since added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, requiring Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to apply the fixes by October 16, 2026.

CISA is also recommending that customers of affected ICS deployments review Ivanti's Connect Secure Upgrade and Migration Compatibility Guide for patching guidance, cautioning that version 22.8 reaches end-of-life on January 31, 2027.

"Organizations seeking to determine whether they were compromised will need to conduct network and memory forensics to identify evidence of exploitation," it added.

In the event a compromise is detected, CISA is advising organizations to implement the following actions -

Create a backup of the appliance configuration.
Conduct a factory reset and upgrade the appliance to the latest version.
For cloud and virtual systems, rebuild the virtual instance and upgrade to the latest version.
Restore the appliance configuration from the backup created in step 1.
Reset passwords for all accounts, including domain, administrator, and local accounts. Revoke and reissue stored certificates; reset stored API keys and license server credentials.

The development comes as Previdian disclosed that it has observed 105 exploitation attempts targeting its honeypot sensors as of October 14, 2026. The attack attempts have originated from 50 unique IP addresses geolocated to Singapore and the U.S. Some of the observed IP addresses are listed below -

216.73.160[.]59
216.73.160[.]61
216.73.160[.]210
45.8.19[.]111

According to Previdian founder and CEO, Ryan Dewhurst, threat actors are using the X-DSCGI-PATH header to reach an internal CGI handler and upload Perl scripts dressed up as ZIP files. The scripts return unique markers that determine whether remote code execution has succeeded.

"We're seeing coordinated attempts to exploit this Ivanti vulnerability, but the payloads captured so far are primarily testing for code execution rather than deploying malware, or compromising the device," Dewhurst told The Hacker News. "However, full weaponized exploitation is likely to follow in the coming hours and days."

In a separate report, Volexity said it first observed the exploitation of CVE-2026-104935 on October 3, 2026, with a previously undocumented threat actor dubbed UTA0576 leveraging it in conjunction with a privilege escalation vulnerability to achieve unauthenticated root-level code execution. UTA0576 is assessed to be driven by criminal motives rather than espionage.

Following successful exploitation, the threat actor is said to have engaged in broad post-exploitation actions, including extracting credentials stored on the ICS VPN appliance, exfiltrating limited Active Directory metadata, deploying a Kerberos tool capable of Kerberoast attacks and credential testing, conducting host reconnaissance, LDAP […]

title: curl Patches HTTP/2 Upload Flaw After PoC Demonstrates Client-Side Code Execution
text:
curl Patches HTTP/2 Upload Flaw After PoC Demonstrates Client-Side Code ExecutionSwati KhandelwalOct 14, 2026Vulnerability / Web Security

//<![CDATA[
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded",()=>{let t=document.querySelector("h1.story-title"),m=document.querySelector(".postmeta");t&&m&&t.insertAdjacentElement("afterend",m)})
//]]>

A flaw in how curl handles HTTP/2 uploads lets a malicious server receiving an upload corrupt the client's memory, and the researcher who reported it turned that into code execution on the uploading machine.

The curl project fixed it on October 14 in curl 8.23.0. Taking over a client needs exact knowledge of its build and memory layout, and curl expects a real attack to end in a crash instead.

The flaw, a use-after-free tracked as CVE-2026-92392, affects curl and libcurl 8.12.0 through 8.22.0, both the command-line tool and the library that many other programs use for transfers. curl rates it High on its own four-level scale, its first High-severity flaw since the SOCKS5 heap overflow of October 2023. The project cut its release cycle by two weeks to ship the fix.

The attack runs from the server side. The client has to upload a file of roughly 135KB over HTTP/2 to a server controlled by the attacker, and the server's certificate must pass the client's checks. libcurl negotiates HTTP/2 by default for https:// URLs when the server offers it, and the library was built with HTTP/2 support.

The flaw has shipped in every curl release since 8.12.0 in February 2025. No source reports attacks that use it. The reporter's HackerOne write-up, with the malicious server script and a Docker container described as reproducing the code execution, became public on October 14 with the advisory.

What to Install, and What to Do Until Then

Upgrade to 8.23.0 or apply the fix commit to a local build. curl's machine-readable advisory also lists fixed versions on three older branches, and the project said it would ship updated Rock-solid curl releases, its long-term-support line for customers with support contracts, in step with 8.23.0:

curl and libcurl 8.12.0 through 8.22.0: upgrade to 8.23.0
8.14.x branch: 8.14.3
8.16.x branch: 8.16.2
8.20.x branch: 8.20.2
Debian 13 (trixie): 8.14.1-2+deb13u7 through DSA-6558-1, per Debian's tracker. Debian 12 (bookworm) does not carry the vulnerable code.

The release fixes 24 CVEs in all. The other 23 are rated Low.

If you cannot update yet, curl's advice is not to use HTTP/2. The --http1.1 option asks the tool for HTTP/1.1, and applications set CURLOPT_HTTP_VERSION to CURL_HTTP_VERSION_1_1. curl's documentation calls that setting a request, because an existing connection on another version may be reused.

HTTP/2 support in libcurl is a build option. A build without it cannot negotiate HTTP/2, so it cannot reach the upload path the advisory describes.

How a Hostile Server Turns the Bug Into Code Execution

Daniel Stenberg, curl's lead developer, explained the bug in a post published with the release, and the public report lays out the code path. HTTP/2 carries several transfers over one connection, and libcurl tracks each transfer with an object it calls an easy handle.

During an upload, the server stalls the transfer by setting the HTTP/2 window to zero, returning part of the response, and then resetting the stream while keeping the connection open. curl treats the reset as a reason to retry.

In cleanup, curl first tells the HTTP/2 layer that the transfer is finished, then flushes the rest of the unsent upload into the same connection. With no transfer registered, those leftover bytes are read as a new request. The line pattern the reporter includes in the uploaded file makes them look like request lines. When they do, a new stream is opened that stores a pointer to the easy handle.

The retry completes on a new HTTP/1.1 connection, and the application frees the handle. The old connection still holds the pointer and uses it when the server sends a frame on that […]

title: Researchers Used a Public OpenAI Model to Build a $250,000 Chrome Full-Chain Exploit in Six Days
text:
Researchers Used a Public OpenAI Model to Build a $250,000 Chrome Full-Chain Exploit in Six DaysSwati KhandelwalOct 14, 2026Vulnerability / Browser Security

//<![CDATA[
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded",()=>{let t=document.querySelector("h1.story-title"),m=document.querySelector(".postmeta");t&&m&&t.insertAdjacentElement("afterend",m)})
//]]>

A team at security firm XBOW chained three then-unknown Google Chrome bugs into a single attack that runs code on a Windows computer when the user only loads a web page, the company said.

Its researchers built the attack in six days by directing AI agents running OpenAI's publicly available GPT-5.6 Sol model. Google has since confirmed all three bugs, fixed them, and paid XBOW its top $250,000 reward for a full Chrome exploit.

The attack is a full chain: a set of bugs used together to break every layer of Chrome's protection, from a web page all the way to the computer.

Chrome runs web page code inside two nested sandboxes, the barriers that stop a hacked page from reaching the rest of the machine. The chain crossed both. The result was code running outside Chrome on Windows, with no need for the user to click or download anything.

All three bugs are now fixed, and XBOW says they were never used against Chrome users. The two that carry public identifiers were fixed in Chrome 152.0.7977.65 on August 25 and 152.0.7977.82 on September 3.

Chrome updates on its own, but the fix only takes effect after the browser restarts, so the action is to relaunch Chrome and confirm the version is 152.0.7977.82 or later.

The six days are the headline, and they need their frame. XBOW built the awarded chain between Sunday, August 2, and Friday, August 7, during the Black Hat and DEF CON conferences in Las Vegas. That sprint followed months of earlier work: the company set the challenge at a January staff meeting in Malta, and its first full Chrome chain took two months to complete.

One version of the awarded chain nearly failed when a bug it relied on turned out to be one Google already knew about. XBOW had built the exploit in swappable parts with backups ready, so it replaced that part and the chain held. By the company's own count of its usage logs, the six-day run cost about $40,000 in AI charges.

XBOW also drew a line between what the AI did and what people did. The AI agents searched Chrome's source code, tested ideas, built proofs of concept, and wrote the first drafts of the exploit. The researchers chose the targets, supplied context, challenged the agents' results, and decided which pieces to join.

One researcher, Brendan Dolan-Gavitt, built the awarded chain with the agents. "Pre-LLMs a Chrome full chain would take a team of four around 6-9 months to be produced, our first submission took 2 months. The awarded one? six days," Dolan-Gavitt wrote.

The three bugs each sat in a different part of Chrome. Google's own release notes credit Dolan-Gavitt of XBOW for two of them and list the version that fixed each.

The first bug gave the attacker control of memory inside Chrome's JavaScript engine.
The second, in the code that reads animated WebP images, used that control to break out of the engine's inner sandbox and make one precise write to the computer's memory.
The third, in Crashpad, Chrome's crash handler, which runs outside the sandbox, turned that single write into full code execution on the machine.

Both identified bugs are rated high severity and need the user to load a page. title: Ivanti vpn-servers volledig gehackt bij aanval, aanvallers zoeken BitLocker keys
text:
Ivanti vpn-servers volledig gehackt bij aanval, aanvallers zoeken BitLocker keys

woensdag 14 oktober 2026, 10:20 door Redactie, 4 reacties

Bij de recente aanvallen tegen Ivanti vpn-servers combineerden de aanvallers drie verschillende kwetsbaarheden om zo volledige controle over de systemen te krijgen. Vervolgens probeerden ze allerlei credentials te stelen, waaronder BitLocker recovery keys. Het Nationaal Cyber Security Centrum (NCSC), het Amerikaanse cyberagentschap CISA en andere overheidsdiensten roepen beheerders en organisaties op om hun Ivanti vpn-servers direct te patchen.

Gisteren kwam Ivanti met beveiligingsupdates voor een kwetsbaarheid in Ivanti Connect Secure (CVE-2026-104935). Ivanti Connect Secure, eerder nog bekend als Pulse Secure, is een vpn-oplossing waarmee gebruikers toegang tot het netwerk van hun organisatie kunnen krijgen. Volgens Ivanti is een 'beperkt aantal' klanten via CVE-2026-104935 gehackt. Details over de aanvallen werden echter niet gegeven.

Cybersecuritybedrijf Volexity ontdekte op 5 oktober een zeroday-aanval op een volledig gepatchte Ivanti vpn-server. Bij de aanval, die op 3 oktober plaatsvond, combineerden de aanvallers een authentication bypass, een remote code execution (RCE) en een privilege escalation kwetsbaarheid om zo ongeauthenticeerd code als root te kunnen uitvoeren. Daarmee wisten de aanvallers volledige controle over de vpn-server te krijgen. De authentication bypass en RCE-kwetsbaarheden hebben CVE-nummer CVE-2026-104935 gekregen.

Vanaf de gehackte vpn-server vielen de aanvallers het achterliggende netwerk aan, aldus Volexity in een analyse van de aanval. Eerst verzamelden de aanvallers alle credentials op de gehackte vpn-server, waaronder domain credentials gebruikt met LDAP, standaard HTTP authentication credentials en NTLM-hashes. Dit werd mede gedaan door het onderscheppen van netwerkverkeer. Ook werd beperkte Active Directory metadata gestolen.

Via een gecompromitteerd Active Directory service account en een zelfgemaakte Python LDAP tool zochten de aanvallers binnen Active Directory ook naar LAPS lokale admin-wachtwoorden, BitLocker recovery keys en 'password-bearing attributes'. Volexity weet niet wie erachter de aanval zit, maar vermoedt dat de aanvallers criminele motieven hebben en het niet om spionage gaat.

Het NCSC beoordeelt de kans op misbruik van het lek en de mogelijke schade als hoog. Organisaties worden dan ook opgeroepen om de patches meteen te installeren. "Een geslaagde aanval kan een kwaadwillende controle geven over het getroffen systeem. Omdat Connect Secure toegang biedt tot de organisatieomgeving, lopen achterliggende systemen en gegevens ook gevaar." Ook het Amerikaanse cyberagentschap CISA, alsmede overheidsdiensten uit andere landen, geven hetzelfde advies.

title: AI-Found Linux Kernel Flaw Gives Local Users Root, and Can Break a Guest Out to the Host
text:
AI-Found Linux Kernel Flaw Gives Local Users Root, and Can Break a Guest Out to the HostSwati KhandelwalOct 14, 2026Vulnerability / Artificial Intelligence

//<![CDATA[
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded",()=>{let t=document.querySelector("h1.story-title"),m=document.querySelector(".postmeta");t&&m&&t.insertAdjacentElement("afterend",m)})
//]]>

A flaw in Linux's vhost subsystem lets a local user read and write kernel memory at will and become root across nearly a decade of kernel versions. In one virtualization setup, it lets an untrusted virtual machine write to the host's memory and hijack the program that runs the virtual machine.

The bug is tracked as CVE-2026-74580 and named Vghost. Tencent Zhuque Lab, which found the flaw, released a fix on August 3 and published a full write-up on October 12 with working demos of both attacks. There is no public sign it has been exploited yet.

vhost is the part of the Linux kernel that speeds up network and other input/output for virtual machines and containers. A local user reaches it by opening a device node, usually /dev/vhost-net or /dev/vhost-vsock.

On the host, the flaw gives an unprivileged user a reliable way to read and write any kernel address, bypass KASLR, and escalate to root. The attack is deterministic: it needs no memory grooming and no lucky timing.

The second attack is narrower. When a virtual machine's virtio device is placed behind a virtual IOMMU with iommu_platform turned on, and vhost runs in device-IOTLB mode, an untrusted guest can trigger the same bug and make the host kernel write out of bounds into the host's QEMU process. From there, a guest can overwrite a function pointer in QEMU and take control of where the host process runs next, or crash it.

How it works

vhost keeps a small cache of the memory mappings behind each virtual ring and the shared queues it uses to move data. A cache hit is treated as proof that the region was already checked. The cache is cleared when the mapping is updated or invalidated and when the queue is reset, but not when the VHOST_SET_VRING_ADDR or VHOST_SET_VRING_NUM commands change the ring's addresses or size while the queue is live.

With a device IOTLB attached, those commands accept the new addresses without checking them, leaving that check for later. Once the cache is filled, the subsequent check never runs, and vhost continues translating new addresses using the old mapping. The kernel then copies data to or from that pointer without a bounds check, so a write to the used ring or a read of a descriptor lands outside the mapped region. That gives the attacker kernel read and write.

The flaw sat in the code for about nine years because it took two reasonable changes to create it. A 2017 change (Linux 4.11) added the cache and its shortcut. A 2020 change (Linux 5.9) moved address checking out of the command and into a later step, removing the check that would otherwise have caught the stale translation.

Who is affected, and what to do

The flaw affects Linux kernels from 4.11 up to 7.2-rc4. Tencent reproduced the full local-user-to-root chain on five distribution kernels: Ubuntu 26.04, RHEL 9.8, Amazon Linux 2023, Microsoft Azure Linux 3.0, and Oracle Linux 10.2. On Ubuntu, the device node was limited to the kvm group, so the starting point there was a member of that group rather than any user.

On the other four tested images, the node was world-readable at mode 0666, so any local user could reach it.

The fix (commit de845981da67) clears the cache whenever the ring is reconfigured. Install a kernel that contains it and reboot. The first fixed upstream stable releases are listed below; vendors may also backport the fix without changing their version number.

title: Microsoft dicht ruim 1400 beveiligingslekken tijdens record Patch Tuesday
text:
Microsoft dicht ruim 1400 beveiligingslekken tijdens record Patch Tuesday

woensdag 14 oktober 2026, 09:16 door Redactie, 20 reacties

Tijdens de Patch Tuesday van oktober heeft Microsoft ruim 1400 beveiligingslekken in de eigen software gepatcht, waaronder een actief aangevallen kwetsbaarheid. Niet eerder dichtte Microsoft tijdens een patchdinsdag zoveel kwetsbaarheden. Elfhonderd van de problemen bevinden zich in Windows, waaronder een beveiligingslek in de Windows Shell (CVE-2026-96951). Dit probleem werd al voor het uitkomen van de patches misbruikt bij aanvallen en maakt het mogelijk om het Mark of the Web te omzeilen.

Mark-of-the-Web (MOTW) is een beveiligingsfeature van Windows die ervoor zorgt dat bestanden die via internet zijn gedownload door Windows van een aparte tag worden voorzien. Bij het openen van bestanden met een MOTW-tag zal Windows een extra waarschuwing aan gebruikers tonen of ze het bestand echt willen openen, aangezien het vanaf internet afkomstig is. Microsoft geeft geen details over de waargenomen aanvallen.

Zo'n honderd van de kwetsbaarheden zijn als kritiek aangemerkt. Het grootste deel van deze problemen bevindt zich in Microsoft Office en maakt remote code execution mogelijk, aldus Microsoft. Misbruik is mogelijk door een gebruiker een speciaal geprepareerd bestand te laten openen, maar in veel gevallen ook via het Voorbeeldvenster (Preview Pane). Dit houdt in dat een doelwit het bestand niet hoeft te openen om misbruik van de kwetsbaarheid te maken.

De meeste beveiligingslekken maken het mogelijk voor een aanvaller die al toegang tot een systeem heeft om zijn rechten te verhogen en zo volledige controle over het systeem te krijgen. Volgens Dustin Childs van cybersecuritybedrijf ZDI zijn 59 van de kwetsbaarheden die Microsoft deze maand heeft verholpen 'wormable', wat inhoudt dat ze zonder interactie van gebruikers zijn te misbruiken en geautomatiseerde aanvallen door een computerworm mogelijk maken.

Een ander probleem dat volgens Childs de aandacht verdient is een kritiek beveiligingslek in Microsoft Office SharePoint (CVE-2026-102866), waardoor een ongeauthenticeerde aanvaller als willekeurige gebruiker kan inloggen, als hij het token van deze gebruiker weet te bemachtigen. Iets wat op verschillende manieren kan. De beveiligingsupdates van Patch Tuesday zullen op de meeste systemen automatisch worden geïnstalleerd.

title: Four-Byte Write and Timing Bug Let Researchers Run Code in Windows SmartScreen Enclave
text:
Four-Byte Write and Timing Bug Let Researchers Run Code in Windows SmartScreen EnclaveSwati KhandelwalOct 14, 2026Vulnerability / Virtualization

//<![CDATA[
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded",()=>{let t=document.querySelector("h1.story-title"),m=document.querySelector(".postmeta");t&&m&&t.insertAdjacentElement("afterend",m)})
//]]>

Security researchers ran their own code inside a protected part of Windows that is meant to stay sealed off even when the rest of the computer is taken over.

The protected area is a VBS enclave, an isolated slice of memory the operating system uses to guard secrets, and the one they broke into handles passwords for a Windows anti-phishing feature.

The work was done in a lab as a proof of concept, has not been seen in real attacks, and Microsoft fixed the flaw in its September 8, 2026 update.

The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-83498. Microsoft rates it an elevation-of-privilege issue, Critical, with a CVSS score of 7.8, and says it has not been exploited and was not publicly known before the fix. Microsoft also says it found the same issue internally. The research, by the security firm Doyensec, was published October 13, more than a month after the patch.

A VBS enclave is a signed library that a normal Windows program loads but cannot read or change once it is running. The Windows hypervisor keeps the enclave's memory in a more trusted world, called VTL1 or Isolated User Mode, that ordinary code in the normal world, VTL0, cannot reach, according to Microsoft.

The design is meant to protect what is inside even if an attacker has already taken over the normal kernel or is running as SYSTEM. Running attacker-chosen code inside that world is what makes this research notable.

The enclave Doyensec attacked is SFAPE.dll, the component behind Enhanced Phishing Protection in Microsoft Defender SmartScreen. That feature watches text you type or paste and warns you if you enter your Windows sign-in password into an unsafe place, such as Notepad or a phishing page.

To do this without exposing the password, Windows intercepts it at login and stores it in hashed form within the enclave, so later inputs can be checked against it. On a Windows 11 system, the program that loads this enclave is lsass.exe, the process that handles sign-in credentials and runs as SYSTEM.

The attack does not work from a distance. It needs a program already running on the machine that loads and calls the enclave; for SFAPE, that's LSASS. Microsoft's own rating says the same: the attack vector is local, and the attacker needs low-level access and no help from the user. In short, this is a way for code that already has a foothold to reach into the more trusted world next to it, not a way in from outside.

Doyensec built the attack from a small mistake and widened it step by step. Calling the enclave's Initialize function a second time makes it write a fixed four-byte error value to an address the calling program controls, and this time it skips the address check the first call performs.

Doyensec is clear that this alone is weak, writing that calling it an arbitrary write "would be a huge overstatement." Aimed at the right spot, though, that one write corrupts the value the enclave uses to tell its own memory from the host's, so its safety check stops working. From there, a timing bug in another function triggers a controlled wipe. That wipe redirects how the enclave looks up a stored object, and the resulting read and write let the researchers replace the table that decides which code the enclave may run.

The result is attacker-chosen code running inside the enclave. The work broke the enclave's isolation; it did not show that a user's password was read or stolen, and Microsoft's advisory describes the impact as data leakage from or code execution inside the enclave.

Microsoft fixed the flaw in the September 8, 2026 cumulative update, KB5124008, for Windows 11 versions 24H2 and 25H2. Doyensec compared the old and new […]

title: Microsoft Patches Record 1,413 Flaws, Including Exploited Windows Shell Bug
text:
Microsoft Patches Record 1,413 Flaws, Including Exploited Windows Shell BugRavie LakshmananOct 14, 2026Vulnerability / Endpoint Security

//<![CDATA[
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded",()=>{let t=document.querySelector("h1.story-title"),m=document.querySelector(".postmeta");t&&m&&t.insertAdjacentElement("afterend",m)})
//]]>

Microsoft on Tuesday shattered its own Patch Tuesday record by shipping patches for a whopping 1,413 vulnerabilities, including one that it said has come under active exploitation.

These include 1,102 flaws in Windows, 134 in Office, 61 in Developer Tools, 36 in SharePoint Server, and 22 in SQL Server. Of these, more than 670 relate to privilege escalation, followed by over 300 remote code execution flaws and 250 information disclosure flaws. Over 70 flaws are rated Critical in severity.

"Hundreds of CVEs in a single release used to be the exception; now it's the baseline," Dustin Childs, head of Threat Awareness at the Zero Day Initiative (ZDI), said. "Is AI to blame? Partly. It's accelerating bug-hunting on both sides of the fence, so vendors are finding (and fixing) more flaws, and researchers are finding them faster too."

"But AI isn't creating these bugs out of thin air; it's just shortening the time between a vulnerability existing and someone noticing it. The volume isn't the real story anymore. What matters is that discovery is scaling faster than exploitation, so teams that triage by sheer CVE count instead of exploitability are burning cycles on the wrong bugs. Patch what's proven, prioritized, and public, and treat everything else as this month's new normal."

The three vulnerabilities of note are listed below -

CVE-2026-96951 (CVSS score: 8.8) - A command injection vulnerability in Windows Shell that allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network.
CVE-2026-108398 (CVSS score: 8.8) - An untrusted search path vulnerability in .NET Framework that allows an authorized attacker to bypass a security feature locally.
CVE-2026-92707 (CVSS score: 5.3) - An improperly controlled sequential memory allocation vulnerability in MessagePack-CSharp that allows an unauthorized attacker to deny service over a network.

Microsoft, which credited Fujitsu's Riku Bamba and Yuya Chudo, as well as Anthropic's Benoit Sevens and a researcher named yhw for reporting CVE-2026-96951, said the vulnerability has been exploited in the wild.

"An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could evade Mark of the Web (MOTW) defenses," the Windows-maker said. "In an email or instant message attack scenario, the attacker could send the targeted user a specially crafted file that is designed to exploit the vulnerability."

"In any case an attacker would have no way to force a user to view attacker-controlled content. Instead, an attacker would have to convince a user to take action. For example, an attacker could entice a user to either click a link that directs the user to the attacker's site or send a malicious attachment."

It's unclear how the vulnerability is being exploited in real-world attacks, by whom, and who has been targeted. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, requiring federal agencies to apply the fixes by October 16, 2026.

CVE-2026-108398 has been acknowledged as publicly known at the time of the release of the patches, with Microsoft stating the security flaw could be exploited to bypass Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) enforcement and run unauthorized applications on target systems.

"An authenticated attacker could place a specially crafted .NET assembly on an affected system and register it for loading by a protected process," Microsoft said. "Successful exploitation could bypass Windows Defender Application Control restrictions and allow the attacker to execute code within the protected process. User interaction is not required."

Microsoft addressed 1,413 vulnerabilities in its October 2026 security update release, including one exploited zero-day vulnerability, two publicly disclosed zero-day vulnerabilities, and 75 Critical vulnerabilities.
October 2026 Risk Analysis
This month's leading risk types by exploitation technique are elevation of privilege with 677 patches (48%), remote code execution (RCE) with 317 patches (22%), and information disclosure with 254 patches (18%).

Figure 1. Breakdown of October 2026 Patch Tuesday exploitation techniques

Windows received the most patches this month with 1,123, followed by ESU with 977 and Microsoft Office with 179.

Figure 2. Breakdown of product families affected by October 2026 Patch Tuesday

October 2026 Attack Surface Analysis
Preview Pane-triggered exploitation dominates this release with 23 CVEs across Office applications including Excel, PowerPoint, and Visio. These flaws require minimal user interaction; a victim could simply view a malicious file in the Reading Pane or file explorer preview, eliminating the traditional click-to-compromise barrier that many enterprises rely on as a user training backstop. The attack surface is substantial; any user who receives a weaponized document via download can trigger code execution simply by selecting the file. This class of flaw has historically been attractive to phishing operators and initial access brokers because it converts document delivery into reliable code execution without requiring macro enablement or a user opening the file.
Unauthenticated network-reachable RCE vulnerabilities appear across 15 CVEs this month, spanning Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) Server, Microsoft Quick UDP Internet Connections (QUIC), PostScript Printer Driver, and PDF handling components. These flaws allow remote attackers to execute code without authentication, making them high-value targets for lateral movement and initial network compromise. DHCP servers in particular are deployed on internal networks by design and trust inbound traffic from any client requesting an address. CVE-2026-100219 and CVE-2026-105016 in Microsoft QUIC represent exposure on any service using QUIC transport, which is increasingly common in modern web infrastructure.
Identity platform components carry critical vulnerabilities this month, with RCE and spoofing flaws affecting both Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) and Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS). CVE-2026-70229 in AD DS enables RCE against domain controllers, while CVE-2026-108131 and CVE-2026-96222 in AD FS present spoofing risks that could enable federated authentication bypass. Compromise of these components can propagate across the entire domain or break trust boundaries between federated identity providers. Similar identity fabric flaws have historically been targeted by advanced adversaries seeking persistent access to enterprise environments.
Microsoft Outlook alone accounts for five critical RCE vulnerabilities this month, including CVE-2026-70242 and CVE-2026-70291, reinforcing email as a persistent high-value attack vector. Outlook's position as the default mail client in most enterprise environments and its deep integration with Exchange and Microsoft 365 services means weaponized messages can reach nearly every employee.

CVE-2026-13762 and CVE-2026-13763 - Issue with HTTP/2 multi-frame request body inspection in AWS WAF

Bulletin ID: 2026-048-AWS
Scope: AWS
Content Type: Important (requires attention)
Publication Date: 06/29/2026 13:15 PM PDT

Description:

AWS WAF is a web application firewall that monitors the HTTP(S) requests that are forwarded to your protected web application resources. We identified CVE-2026-13762 and CVE-2026-13763, which are issues affecting HTTP/2 multi-frame request body inspection by AWS WAF.

CVE-2026-13762 affects AWS WAF deployment with CloudFront. This issue was remediated server-side; no customer action is required.

CVE-2026-13763 affects AWS WAF deployment with AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB). Under certain conditions, a crafted multi-frame HTTP/2 request could cause only a partial request body to be inspected. This issue has been addressed on ALB, and customers can ensure full protection by configuring how AWS WAF inspects HTTP/2 request bodies on their ALB.

Resolution:

On May 22, 2026, we released a new configuration option on ALB, which addresses this issue. We recommend that customers review and update the WAF HTTP/2 traffic inspection behavior under target group attributes for HTTP/2 endpoints. This enables ALB to accumulate HTTP/2 data frames before AWS WAF performs inspection. For detailed instructions, refer to the developer guide.

Workarounds:

No workarounds are available.

References:

CVE-2026-13762
CVE-2026-13763

Acknowledgement:

We would like to thank Kyungrok Choi, Woonghee Lee, and Junbeom Hur from Korea University ISSLab for collaborating on these issues through the coordinated vulnerability disclosure process.

Please email aws-security@amazon.com with any security questions or concerns.

Issue with FreeRTOS-Plus-TCP - MAC Address Validation Bypass and ICMP Echo Reply Integer Underflow

Bulletin ID: 2026-021-AWS
Scope: AWS
Content Type: Important (requires attention)
Publication Date: 04/29/2026 11:45 AM PDT

Description:

FreeRTOS-Plus-TCP is a scalable, open source, and thread-safe TCP/IP stack for FreeRTOS.

CVE-2026-7422: Insufficient packet validation in the IPv4 and IPv6 receive paths allows an adjacent network device to send a packet that bypasses checksum and minimum-size validation by spoofing the Ethernet source MAC address to match one of the target device's own registered endpoints.
CVE-2026-7423: Integer underflow in the ICMP and ICMPv6 echo reply handlers allows an adjacent network device to cause a denial of service (device crash) when outgoing ping support is enabled, because header sizes are subtracted from a packet length field without validating the field is large enough, resulting in a heap out-of-bounds read.

Impacted versions: >=V4.0.0 AND <=V4.2.5, >=V4.3.0 AND <=V4.4.0

Resolution:

This issue has been addressed in FreeRTOS-Plus-TCP version V4.4.1 and V4.2.6. We recommend upgrading to the latest version and ensuring any forked or derivative code is patched to incorporate the new fixes.

Workarounds:

CVE-2026-7422 (ICMP integer underflow) can be mitigated by disabling outgoing ping support by setting ipconfigSUPPORT_OUTGOING_PINGS to 0 in your FreeRTOSIPConfig.h configuration file, or by updating to a fixed version. Mitigating CVE-2026-7423 (MAC address validation bypass) requires updating to a fixed version.

References:

CVE-2026-7422
CVE-2026-7423
GHSA-jpw4-6h59-62w9
GHSA-7r59-2pgv-9v2r

Acknowledgment:

We would like to thank Espilon for collaborating on this issue through the coordinated vulnerability disclosure process.

CVE-2026-8596 & CVE-2026-8597: Issue with Amazon SageMaker Python SDK - Model artifact integrity verification issues

Bulletin ID: 2026-031-AWS
Scope: AWS
Content Type: Important (requires attention)
Publication Date: 05/14/2026 12:45 PM PDT

Description:

Amazon SageMaker Python SDK is an open-source library for training and deploying machine learning models on Amazon SageMaker. The ModelBuilder component simplifies model deployment by automating model artifact preparation and SageMaker model creation.

We identified two issues affecting the model artifact integrity verification mechanism in the ModelBuilder/Serve component:

CVE-2026-8596: We identified a cleartext storage of sensitive information issue in the ModelBuilder/Serve component. When building models using ModelBuilder, the SDK stored an HMAC signing key as a container environment variable (SAGEMAKER_SERVE_SECRET_KEY). This key was returned in plaintext by SageMaker describe APIs (DescribeModel, DescribeEndpointConfig, DescribeModelPackage). A remote authenticated actor with permissions to call these APIs and S3 write access to the model artifact path could extract the key, forge valid integrity signatures for specially crafted model artifacts, and achieve code execution in inference containers.

CVE-2026-8597: We identified a missing integrity verification issue in the Triton inference handler. The Triton handler deserialized model artifacts without performing integrity verification before execution. A remote authenticated actor with S3 write access to the model artifact path could replace model artifacts with a specially crafted pickle payload that would be deserialized without verification, achieving code execution in inference containers.

Impacted versions: Amazon SageMaker Python SDK >= v2.199.0 AND <= v2.257.1, >= v3.0.0 AND <= v3.7.1

Resolution:

These issues have been addressed in Amazon SageMaker Python SDK v2.257.2 and v3.8.0. We recommend upgrading to the latest version and rebuilding any models previously created with ModelBuilder using the updated SDK. Models created with affected versions may still have the HMAC key stored in their container environment variables until they are rebuilt with the patched SDK.

Workarounds:

If upgrading is not immediately possible, users can manually remove the SAGEMAKER_SERVE_SECRET_KEY environment variable from existing SageMaker models by recreating the model without this variable in the container environment configuration. Additionally, users should restrict S3 write access to model artifact paths to only trusted principals.

References:

CVE-2026-8596
CVE-2026-8597
GHSA-7hh5-prp2-mfh5
GHSA-rq6v-x3j8-7qgf

CVE-2026-15746 - Credential disclosure in Strands Agents Tools elasticsearch_memory tool

Bulletin ID: 2026-056-AWS
Scope: AWS
Content Type: Important (requires attention)
Publication Date: 07/15/2026 11:30 AM PDT

Description:

Strands Agents is an open-source Python SDK for building and running AI agents. The strands-agents-tools package provides pre-built tools for use with the SDK, including the elasticsearch_memory tool for agent memory storage. We identified CVE-2026-15746, a server-side request forgery (SSRF) issue in the elasticsearch_memory tool. The tool exposed its connection parameters (es_url, cloud_id, api_key) as fields the large language model (LLM) could control through the tool schema. When a caller omitted the api_key parameter, the tool fell back to the operator's ELASTICSEARCH_API_KEY environment variable and sent it to whichever host the LLM specified. A crafted prompt could cause the tool to connect to a threat-actor-controlled server and disclose the operator's Elasticsearch API key in the Authorization header.

Impacted versions: < 0.7.0

Resolution:

This issue has been addressed in strands-agents-tools version 0.7.0. We recommend upgrading to the latest version and ensuring any forked or derivative code is patched to incorporate the new fixes. As a precautionary measure, we recommend all operators rotate their ELASTICSEARCH_API_KEY, even if there is no indication the credential was exposed.

Workarounds:

Avoid using the elasticsearch_memory tool until you upgrade to version 0.7.0 or later. If you must continue running an affected version, do not expose the ELASTICSEARCH_API_KEY environment variable to the tool, and restrict outbound network access so the agent host can reach only your trusted Elasticsearch endpoint.

References:

CVE-2026-15746
GHSA-ppcf-fpr3-x46v

Please email aws-security@amazon.com with any security questions or concerns.

Issue with containerd CRI Plugin - CVE-2026-50195, CVE-2026-53488, CVE-2026-53492, CVE-2026-53489, CVE-2026-47262

Bulletin ID: 2026-046-AWS
Scope: AWS
Content Type: Important (requires attention)
Publication Date: 06/18/2026 17:30 PM PDT
Last Updated Date: 6/22/2026 15:00 PM PDT

Description:

containerd is an open-source container runtime used by Kubernetes via the Container Runtime Interface (CRI) plugin. It underpins AWS managed container services including Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS), Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), AWS Fargate, Bottlerocket, and Amazon Linux. AWS identified five issues in the containerd CRI plugin affecting versions 1.7 through 2.3

CVE-2026-50195 (CVSS 8.8): Unvalidated checkpoint image references in the CRI plugin allow image cache poisoning on shared Kubernetes nodes, enabling cross-pod code execution.
CVE-2026-53488 (CVSS 8.3): Image configuration LABEL instructions are propagated to containers without sanitization, enabling arbitrary host command execution via a crafted container image. This issue does not require checkpoint/restore to be enabled.
CVE-2026-53492 (CVSS 6.8): CDI (Container Device Interface) annotations from untrusted checkpoint image metadata are trusted without validation, allowing device and host mount injection that bypasses Kubernetes device enforcement. This issue requires CDI to be enabled on the node.
CVE-2026-53489 (CVSS 6.5): Symlinked container log paths are not validated during checkpoint restore, enabling arbitrary host file read. This issue requires checkpoint/restore to be enabled.
CVE-2026-47262 (CVSS 6.5): A crafted container image can cause uncontrolled memory consumption, resulting in an out-of-memory termination of the containerd process and a denial of service for all containers on the affected node.

Impacted versions: containerd 1.7, 2.0, 2.1, 2.2, 2.3

Resolution:

These issues have been addressed in the upstream containerd project. Patched releases are available at the containerd GitHub security advisories page. We recommend upgrading to the latest patched version and ensuring any forked or derivative code is updated to incorporate the new fixes.

For customers using AWS managed container services (Amazon EKS, Amazon ECS, AWS Fargate), AWS is deploying patched runtimes across affected fleets. Customers using self-managed containerd deployments on Amazon EC2 or on-premises infrastructure should upgrade to a patched container version as soon as possible.

Workarounds:

CVE-2026-47262: Users can mitigate this issue by only allowing trusted images to be pulled and only allowing trusted users to import images and schedule pods.
CVE-2026-50195 and CVE-2026-53488: Users can mitigate this issue by only allowing trusted images to be pulled.
CVE-2026-53489: Users can mitigate this issue by only allowing trusted images to be pulled and only restoring from trusted checkpoints.

CVE-2026-16317 and CVE-2026-16318: Issues with s2n-tls: an open-source implementation of the TLS/SSL protocols

Bulletin ID: 2026-062-AWS
Scope: AWS
Content Type: Important (requires attention)
Publication Date: 07/21/2026 13:00 PM PDT

Description:

s2n-tls is an open source C99 implementation of the TLS/SSL protocol. We have identified two distinct issues:

CVE-2026-16317: Silent Drop of TLS 1.3 Encrypted Records in s2n-tls
Missing validation of the outer content_type byte on TLS 1.3 encrypted records in s2n-tls allows an active man-in-the-middle to silently drop individual application data records without either endpoint detecting the modification. RFC 8446 Section 5.2 requires that the outer content_type of all encrypted TLS 1.3 records must be application_data (0x17). The s2n-tls AEAD implementation hardcodes this value in the additional authenticated data rather than using the actual wire byte, so the outer content_type is not covered by the authentication tag. All TLS 1.3 connections are affected. Both TLS clients and servers are affected. TLS 1.2 and QUIC connections are not affected.

CVE-2026-16318: QUIC Transport Parameters Memory Leak During HelloRetryRequest in s2n-tls
Incorrect use of s2n_alloc instead of s2n_realloc in the QUIC transport parameters extension handler in s2n-tls causes one memory allocation to be leaked each time a QUIC-enabled TLS 1.3 connection goes through a HelloRetryRequest. This can occur during normal handshakes when a client offers a key share group the server does not prefer, and can lead to increased memory consumption on long-running server processes. Only QUIC-enabled deployments are affected.

Impacted versions: <= v1.7.5

Resolution:

These issues have been addressed in s2n-tls version v1.7.6. We recommend upgrading to the latest version and ensuring any forked or derivative code is patched to incorporate the new fixes.

Workarounds:

For CVE-2026-16317 (Silent Drop of TLS 1.3 Encrypted Records), there is no workaround that fully mitigates this issue. Configuring s2n-tls to use only TLS 1.2 security policies would avoid the affected code path, but this is not recommended as it removes the security benefits of TLS 1.3.

For CVE-2026-16318 (QUIC Transport Parameters Memory Leak During HelloRetryRequest), deployments that do not enable QUIC are not affected and do not require any action. For QUIC-enabled deployments, restarting server processes periodically can reclaim the unreachable memory as a temporary mitigation.

References:

CVE-2026-16317
CVE-2026-16318
GHSA-cr7x-863j-xrc7
GHSA-684c-v35q-fvx7

CVE-2026-15737 - Sensitive content disclosure via OpenTelemetry spans in AgentCore Python SDK

Bulletin ID: 2026-058-AWS
Scope: AWS
Content Type: Important (requires attention)
Publication Date: 07/16/2026 10:00 AM PDT

Description:

Bedrock AgentCore Python SDK (bedrock-agentcore) is an open-source Python library that provides client tools for building AI agents on the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore platform. We identified CVE-2026-15737 in the OpenTelemetry instrumentation of the SDK. Affected versions wrote raw user prompts and complete agent responses into OpenTelemetry span attributes on every invocation without filtering or masking. These spans flow into the customer's aws/spans CloudWatch log group, where a local authenticated user with CloudWatch Logs read access could access the potentially sensitive content.

Impacted versions: 1.4.8, 1.5.0

Resolution:

This issue has been addressed in Bedrock AgentCore Python SDK version 1.5.1 or later. We recommend upgrading to the latest version and ensuring any forked or derivative code is patched to incorporate the new fixes. Users who ran affected versions should also review and purge sensitive content from their aws/spans CloudWatch log groups.

Workarounds:

No workarounds are available. Upgrade Bedrock AgentCore Python SDK to version 1.5.1 or later.

References:

CVE-2026-15737

CVE-2026-5747 - Out-of-bounds Write in Firecracker virtio-pci Transport

Bulletin ID: 2026-015-AWS
Scope: AWS
Content Type: Important
Publication Date: 04/7/2026 3:30 PM PST

Description:

Firecracker is an open source virtualization technology that is purpose-built for creating and managing secure, multi-tenant container and function-based services.

We identified CVE-2026-5747, an out-of-bounds write issue in the virtio PCI transport in Firecracker 1.13.0 through 1.14.3 and 1.15.0 on x86_64 and aarch64 that might allow a local guest user with root privileges to crash the Firecracker VMM process or potentially execute arbitrary code on the host via modification of virtio queue configuration registers after device activation. Achieving code execution on the host requires additional preconditions, such as the use of a custom guest kernel or specific snapshot configurations.

No AWS service is affected.

Impacted versions: Firecracker >= 1.13.0 AND <= 1.14.3 AND 1.15.0

Resolution:

This issue has been addressed in Firecracker version 1.14.4 and 1.15.1. We recommend upgrading to the latest version and ensuring any forked or derivative code is patched to incorporate the new fixes.

Workarounds
The virtio PCI transport is opt-in via the --enable-pci command-line flag when starting Firecracker. The legacy MMIO transport is the default and is not affected by this issue. Users who have enabled PCI transport can revert to MMIO by removing the --enable-pci flag from their Firecracker invocation. Note that switching from PCI to MMIO transport may result in reduced I/O throughput and increased latency.

References
CVE-2026-5747
GHSA-776c-mpj7-jm3r

Acknowledgement
We thank Anthropic for reporting this concern to the AWS Vulnerability Disclosure Program.

Please email aws-security@amazon.com with any security questions or concerns.

We identified CVE-2026-9255, an issue where missing input source validation in the tool authorization prompt could allow a local actor to execute arbitrary tools, including shell commands, without user approval by crafting content that is piped to kiro-cli via stdin.

Run kiro-cli with the --no-interactive flag when piping content from untrusted sources. This explicitly disables tool approval prompts and prevents piped input from being consumed as confirmation responses.

Description:

AWS Ops Wheel is an open-source tool that helps teams make random selections using a virtual spinning wheel, deployed into customer AWS accounts via CloudFormation.

CVE-2026-6911 relates to an issue where JWT token signature verification was not enforced in the v2 API. This could allow an unauthenticated actor with network access to the API Gateway endpoint to craft a token and gain unintended administrative access to the application, including the ability to read, modify, and delete all application data across tenants and manage Cognito user accounts within the deployment's User Pool.

This could allow an authenticated user to modify their own privilege attributes and gain elevated access within the application, including the ability to manage Cognito user accounts.

Impacted versions:

AWS Ops Wheel v2 deployments PR #163 and earlier

CVE-2026-6911 has been addressed in PR #164 and CVE-2026-6912 has been addressed in PR #165. Users should redeploy from the latest version and ensure any forked or derivative code is patched to incorporate the new fixes.

Workarounds:

Customers who cannot immediately redeploy can restrict network access to their API Gateway endpoint using AWS WAF or VPC configurations to limit access.

Bulletin ID: 2026-052-AWS
Scope: AWS
Content Type: Important (requires attention)
Publication Date: 07/06/2026 13:45 PM PDT

Description:

Amazon mcp-gateway-registry is an open-source gateway and registry for Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, providing centralized discovery, authentication/authorization, and proxying of MCP tools for AI agents. We identified CVE-2026-14471, an issue in the metrics-service retention policy management component where a caller-supplied table_name value is interpolated into SQL statements in identifier position without proper neutralization. An authenticated remote user is able to supply a crafted table_name value to execute arbitrary SQL queries against the metrics database. This allows the user to read stored data (including API key material) and to delete or alter stored data.

Impacted versions: >=1.0.3 AND <=1.0.12

Resolution:

This issue has been addressed in mcp-gateway-registry version 1.0.13. We recommend upgrading to the latest version and ensuring any forked or derivative code is patched to incorporate the new fixes.

Workarounds:

There is no workaround. Upgrade to version 1.0.13 or later; please check the GitHub repository for the latest release.

CVE-2026-15643 - AWS HealthLake MCP Server SSRF via Unvalidated Pagination URL

Bulletin ID: 2026-054-AWS
Scope: AWS
Content Type: Important (requires attention)
Publication Date: 07/14/2026 13:00 PM PDT

Description:

AWS HealthLake MCP Server (awslabs.healthlake-mcp-server) is a Model Context Protocol server that enables AI assistants to interact with AWS HealthLake FHIR datastores. We identified CVE-2026-15643 a server-side request forgery in the pagination handling component in AWS awslabs.healthlake-mcp-server before 0.0.14 on all platforms might allow a remote authenticated user to exfiltrate AWS temporary security credentials to an arbitrary endpoint via a crafted next_token parameter. The server does not validate that pagination URLs point back to the expected HealthLake endpoint, allowing an actor to redirect subsequent requests to an actor-controlled server.

Impacted versions: < 0.0.14

Resolution:

This issue has been addressed in awslabs.healthlake-mcp-server version 0.0.14. We recommend upgrading to the latest version and ensuring any forked or derivative code is patched to incorporate the new fixes.

Workarounds:

In the interim, scope the IAM policy used by the server to least privilege rather than Resource: "*", and do not rely on the --readonly flag as a security boundary — it is an in-process guard over the mutating tools, not an IAM control, so disclosed credentials retain their full granted authority. Operators using role-based (STS) deployments should consider rotating the affected role's credentials if they suspect using an affected version.

References:

CVE-2026-15643
GHSA-c5vr-x62j-w6rw

We would like to thank Marios Gyftos for collaborating on this issue through the coordinated vulnerability disclosure process.
